scope: Bounded manual map of current documented GNU option inventory and implementation routing. Every group has native passthrough when its full command is unqualified; this is not enumeration of the unbounded regex, argv, locale or filesystem universe.

claims.scopeOfDocumentedInterface: 47 semantic option groups from the captured GNU help/manual inventory; future/unknown options pass through to installed GNU.

inventory.countMeaning: Spelling/group/case inventory counts, not percentage of GNU semantics or universal correctness.

routes.contract: Actual rg evaluates original selected file/stream contents and its results determine selected-record status/output. JSON mode applies the GNU formatter; narrow fixed -l direct mode inherits rg streams. Local literal span rendering can supplement rg without a GNU original-input search.

Actual rg selects original-input records. Private spools contain rg match/context events and those candidate record bytes; GNU computes only their exact extraction/highlight spans, and the formatter restores original offsets/filenames. GNU never receives original file operands in this broker.
routes.speedCaveat: Match-heavy inputs, disk spooling and a second candidate pass may be slower than direct GNU.

routes.contract: Actual rg selects records from bounded positional reads of a single explicit-text regular FD0 under finite positive -m. Original shared cursor advances only to the completed GNU position; -A does not advance it past the final selected record. No whole-suffix spool or disk writes.
routes.speedCaveat: Streaming and forward cursor advancement add reads; interruption timing and concurrent updates of the same open file description are outside the completed-command oracle.

routes.contract: Execute installed GNU with original argv and inherited streams; preserve unsupported semantics and diagnostics. Preparation may previously have read metadata/text or run compile/calibration probes, but those do not make final native output rg acceleration.

contributionAccounting.plannedBackendRg: A proposal from planGrep; preparation or availability checks may still select native. Never sufficient evidence of acceleration.
contributionAccounting.actualInputContribution: Require a real rg invocation over original selected operands/stream that determines selected results/status or candidate records used in final output, with no original-argv GNU search replacing those results. A zero-match completed real search can still contribute status1; report its outcome separately from matching-result contribution.
contributionAccounting.compileProbes: GNU /dev/null compilation and rg empty-input compilation validate semantics/dependencies only. Count separately; no original input contribution.
contributionAccounting.unicodeCalibration: GNU version/identity checks, exhaustive valid-scalar synthetic corpus membership and separate NUL membership calibrate tables only. Count separately; they do not accelerate original operands by themselves.
contributionAccounting.hybridBroker: GNU over candidate-records is semantic span evaluation and must be reported separately from original-argv GNU fallback.
contributionAccounting.discardedRg: Compile-only, aborted/failed, compatibility-rejected or native-replaced rg work receives no successful accelerated-result credit.
contributionAccounting.testing: Independent test recorders distinguish real rg, GNU candidate broker, GNU compile/scalar probes and original GNU searches; fault/mutant executions are verification work, not product acceleration.

globalQualification.appliesTo: Every conditional option profile together with its full option sequence, operands, input bytes and environment. Individual option support never qualifies every combination.
globalQualification.ordinaryInputContract: Output bytes, diagnostics and exit status on qualified stable inputs; no claim of identical syscall/access/atime timing or atomic filesystem snapshots.
globalQualification.fallbackBeforeOutput: Parser/preparation qualifications choose original GNU before matching output and before consuming caller stdin. File metadata/text reads and synthetic calibration can occur before native selection.
globalQualification.postSearch: Search/broker/protocol failures cannot safely restart original input after output or stdin consumption; controlled error paths and cleanup apply.

matcher-posix.contract: Translate qualified BRE/ERE to PCRE2 for record selection; literal expressions may use fixed matching. General extraction/highlighting resolves GNU leftmost-longest spans only on rg-selected/context records.

matcher-fixed.contract: Select records with fixed matching or GNU-proved scalar closures; literal leftmost-longest rendering is local when qualified, otherwise extraction/highlighting can use candidate-only GNU spans.

matcher-perl.contract: Use installed rg PCRE2 for qualified C/POSIX Perl expressions after empty-input compilation.

pattern.contract: Preserve additive newline-separated patterns and pattern-local numbered capture groups; required option values remain patterns.

pattern-file.contract: Resolve qualified ordinary UTF-8 pattern files before searching; preserve empty-file shortcuts and native stream/error ownership.

case.contract: Preserve last-option case policy; C/POSIX byte semantics or proved GNU UTF-8 scalar folding determine actual rg selection.

word.contract: Implement GNU adjacent word-character tests, including non-word patterns, using byte classes or GNU scalar membership.

line.contract: Match complete LF/NUL records with record-aware anchors; NUL records may contain embedded LF.

null-data.contract: Use NUL record delimiters and preserve embedded LF, record numbers, offsets, extraction and context.

no-messages.contract: Suppress search diagnostics as requested; discovery errors still select original GNU before actual matching.

invert.contract: Preserve selected-record status independently from emitted extraction, counts and filenames.

informational.contract: Execute original GNU arguments for GNU help/version and option diagnostic precedence.

max-count.contract: Preserve per-file selected-record limits and trailing context using rg selection and formatter state.

prefix.contract: Format raw byte offsets, line/record numbers, original filename labels and GNU match/context delimiters.

line-buffered.contract: Write qualified formatter output incrementally with stdout backpressure. Candidate-span rendering starts after its rg batch and GNU span pass.

filename.contract: Preserve last H/h policy, GNU default filename decisions and recursive operand labels.

label.contract: Preserve the original stdin label and raw UTF-8 display bytes for qualified streams.

extraction.contract: Use local literal longest-span rendering when eligible; general POSIX spans come from GNU over rg candidates rather than original operands.

quiet.contract: Preserve quiet output suppression and selected-match/error precedence; qualified file searches can stop after a selected record.

binary-policy.contract: Explicit text searches select rg directly where qualified; default binary reporting and without-match require complete selected-file text proof, except the narrow fixed filename direct route.

directories.contract: Preserve read/recurse/skip policy and option ordering; selected directory errors use original GNU.

devices.contract: Preserve read/skip choice and command-line versus descended special-file rules; selected readable special files use GNU.

recursive.contract: Enumerate GNU-selected regular files in native directory order, including hidden/ignored files; preserve command-line symlink behavior.

recursive-follow.contract: Follow interior symlinks while retaining GNU ordering and cycle diagnostics through original GNU fallback.

filter.contract: Apply ordered last-matching include/exclude rules with command-line suffix versus descended basename semantics; braces remain literals.

exclude-file.contract: Expand qualified exclusion files at their original position among include/exclude rules.

files-mode.contract: Preserve last l/L policy, emitted filename decisions, NUL filename delimiters and selected-record status. A narrow fixed -l regular-file route uses inherited rg streams.

count.contract: Count selected records per file, including zero counts and max-count/invert interactions.

initial-tab.contract: Format GNU tab-aligned numeric prefixes using the selected file size and record information.

null-names.contract: Emit NUL after filename prefixes/listings independently of the LF/NUL record delimiter.

context.contract: Preserve explicit A/B precedence over generic C/numeric defaults, selected/context delimiters, adjacent groups and zero-context group separators.

separator.contract: Preserve repeated separator/no-separator ordering and raw separator output.

color.contract: Preserve never/auto/always, TERM and GREP_COLORS capabilities; qualified POSIX highlighting uses exact candidate spans.

platform-binary.contract: Linux -U/--binary is a GNU no-op and preserves the otherwise qualified rg route; other platforms retain original GNU byte-mode handling.

nativeBoundaries.condition: Unknown/ambiguous options, missing values, conflicting matcher history, invalid required values or GNU help/version behavior use original GNU arguments. Exact long names and unique long abbreviations are parsed; getopt permutation obeys POSIXLY_CORRECT.

Public Bash and private function preserve original invalid UTF-8 argv bytes by running GNU before Node argument decoding. Valid UTF-8 argv can qualify. Direct Node string APIs cannot recover bytes already replaced by decoding.
Unavailable /proc/self/cwd, deleted cwd or invalid UTF-8 raw cwd runs original GNU with the inherited OS cwd before parser/file reads.

Linux is the qualified deployment; GNU -U/--binary is a no-op here and retains the otherwise qualified rg route. Windows and non-Linux binary translation use original GNU. Linux /proc, Bash, GNU readlink, Node >=24, GNU grep and usable rg are runtime dependencies; missing rg runs GNU.

Explicit-text, finite positive -m can use rg for one implicit stdin or one single - operand when FD0 is a readable, seekable, stable regular file with honest declared size. 64 KiB positional reads stream to rg without moving the shared cursor; normal completion then consumes the original only up to GNU's selected-record end, or EOF when the limit is not reached. -q/-l/-L, repeated or mixed stdin operands, pipes/FIFOs/sockets, O_PATH/O_DIRECT, dishonest proc/sysfs sizes, default binary handling, Unicode/ASCII proof-dependent streams and -f - retain original GNU.

Only optional + followed by decimal digits qualifies; other GNU-version-specific spellings, negative values, whitespace and values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER remain native. Contiguous numeric short-option runs are generic context defaults; intervening letters end a run.
-m 0 performs GNU validation/output directly and receives no rg contribution credit.

Pattern/exclusion files must resolve to ordinary regular files or ordinary symlinks to regular files, be <=1 MiB, complete valid UTF-8 and contain no NUL. Stdin pattern files, read failures, special files, oversized/invalid byte contents, empty aggregate pattern sets and expansion bounds use GNU.

Unsupported/invalid BRE/ERE grammar stays GNU: collation/equivalence elements, GNU stray-backslash warnings, invalid POSIX class names/brackets, trailing escapes, unmatched groups, leading/repeated quantifiers, invalid interval syntax/order or repetitions >32767, PCRE-only ERE group extensions and different numbered-backreference parsing. Translation/PCRE2 compilation failure stays GNU before actual subject search.

Perl matching qualifies only in C/POSIX and without NUL-data. UTF-8/non-C Perl behavior, Perl -z, more than one distinct pattern, repeated-pattern matcher construction failures and unavailable/incompatible PCRE2 remain native.

C/POSIX use byte rules. Supported UTF-8 non-Perl searches can require complete valid-UTF-8 file proof and GNU scalar membership tables for folding/words/classes; a proved ASCII C.UTF-8 shortcut avoids corpus calibration. Non-UTF-8 regex encodings, insensitive backreferences, unsupported membership probes and multi-character locale collation remain native. Unicode bracket matching requires C/POSIX/C.UTF-8 collation. Effective LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LC_COLLATE/LANG precedence is retained.
Inverted empty-pattern universal shortcuts without word/line restriction retain native GNU behavior.

GNU /dev/null span compilation must complete with status0/1, no signal/error and empty stderr before rg search. Any diagnostic, warning, timeout or failed compilation triggers original GNU. GNU candidate span execution after search is hybrid semantic work, not a second original-input search.

Default binary/without-match JSON routes require complete ordinary-file text classification. C/POSIX rejects NUL unless -z makes it the delimiter; UTF-8 also rejects malformed sequences. Unicode scalar selection always requires complete valid-UTF-8 proof, even with -a. The narrow fixed filename direct route retains rg binary mode instead of this classification. Replacement/FIFO/mutation observed during proof selects GNU.

A selected special input, stat/open/traversal error, recursive cycle or discovered invalid-UTF-8 filename selects original GNU before output. Device skip and directory skip may exclude those inputs according to GNU rules. No atomic snapshot exists between discovery/text proof and rg reopening operands.
Exact read/recurse/skip values can qualify. GNU accepted ACTION abbreviations are preserved through original GNU, because this parser accepts only exact values.
Exact read/skip values can qualify; invalid or release-specific values use GNU.

Unicode filename-glob arguments and collating/equivalence glob elements remain native. POSIX filename classes and ranges require both effective CTYPE and COLLATE to be C/POSIX. Ordinary ASCII literal/star/question/bracket globs otherwise use qualified adapter file selection; full root/suffix/basename semantics are independent of rg ignore rules.

Invalid WHEN runs GNU help behavior. Auto color depends on actual stdout TTY and TERM. GNU capabilities come from GREP_COLORS; highlight spans require qualified local literal or candidate-only GNU selection.

Public/private Bash snapshots caller auxiliary descriptors before Node/libuv changes CLOEXEC flags; GNU/rg children inherit still-open listed and observable non-CLOEXEC descriptors. Closed standard0/1/2 run GNU before Node opens /dev/null replacements. Direct Node APIs lack the pre-Node Bash snapshot and cannot reconstruct inherited low descriptors already marked CLOEXEC.
Exact numeric resource limits are recorded below. Crossing preparation bounds retains original GNU before output; there is no obsolete16MiB payload/4096-file text-proof cutoff.

After actual rg search starts, errors/protocol faults/candidate-broker failure use controlled error status and cleanup; there is no unsafe original-input restart after output or stream consumption. Underlying rg runtime diagnostics can surface. Stable-input oracle comparisons do not prove race/error/interleaving equivalence.

resourceLimits.comparison: native if sum > value; payload bytes are not included

resourceLimits.unit: UTF-8 bytes plus one terminator per argument
resourceLimits.comparison: full direct-route argv and matching-argument arrays checked separately; JSON operand batches have an independent label-byte budget, not a combined49152-byte full argv guarantee
working read chunk; complete files read to EOF with no aggregate payload cutoff
larger accepted decimal values use native original values rather than saturated JS counters
larger BRE/ERE interval endpoints use native
failed GNU span or rg PCRE/Unicode compile uses native

resourceLimits.contains: Every valid nonzero Unicode scalar once, separated by NUL; excludes surrogates; NUL itself gets a separate probe.

resourceLimits.comparison: larger table ignored and recalibrated; no global table-count/cache-size bound

resourceLimits.unit: JS string code units per search/broker stderr capture
resourceLimits.comparison: tail beyond cap discarded; not a byte count or GNU diagnostic equivalence claim under fault injection
SIGKILL timer for still-running owned active child after HUP/INT/TERM; not a general daemon containment guarantee
No automatic duration limit for actual rg searches or GNU candidate span evaluation; cancellation applies.
No fixed input-record/JSON-event size cap; current-record buffers/pending JSON can grow with one large record. Backpressure limits queued output, not arbitrary record size.
No fixed aggregate candidate/event/span spool byte cap; private disk usage grows with selected/context records and spans, and owned spools are removed after replay/cancellation.

genuineNativeExamples.reason: Shared stream cannot be positionally read and restored; ordinary qualified regular stdin can instead use rg.
genuineNativeExamples.inputKind: pipe, FIFO or another unqualified stdin descriptor

genuineNativeExamples.reason: Cannot pre-read caller stdin to prove binary classification
Installed GNU handles version-specific numeric spelling
Bash preserves raw bytes and runs GNU
Adapter cannot reconstruct decoded original label
GNU multi-character bracket collation, when that locale is installed

configurationAndScope.publicCli: bin/grep2rg accepts original GNU argv. Default executes GNU immediately; explicit experimental routes use Bash/readlink byte, symlink and descriptor guards.
configurationAndScope.shellPrefix: bin/grep2rg-shell-prefix.mjs prints an absolute-path Bash definition for the caller; withGrepWrapper prepends it only for eligible Bash contexts. Function grep is explicitly not exported; command grep, absolute paths and child shells use ordinary lookup.
configurationAndScope.pi: Normal native Bash has no hook. Exact experimental opt-in plus allowed provider enables the model-only wrapper; user shell execution remains native.
configurationAndScope.unicodeCache: GREP2RG_UNICODE_CACHE overrides private cache directory; otherwise OS temp/grep2rg-unicode-UID. Require user-owned real directory with no group/other permissions. Corpus/tables use0600 files, identity/checksum validation and atomic replacement. Custom LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH/LOCPATH disable persistent and cross-request memory reuse.
configurationAndScope.callerDescriptors: _GREP2RG_CALLER_FDS is private one-shot Bash snapshot metadata, consumed/deleted before child execution; no arbitrary4096 descriptor-number cap. Node-only APIs cannot retroactively preserve already-decoded argv, already-reopened standard descriptors or low descriptors without the launcher snapshot.
configurationAndScope.signals: JSON execution handles SIGHUP/SIGINT/SIGTERM with cancellation status129/130/143, active-child cleanup and broker spool cleanup. Public/private CLI exits after cancellation cleanup; runGrep API returns status without terminating its caller. Inherited direct/native routes preserve their own ordinary process behavior.

limitations: Potential rg route is not universal acceleration or measured speedup. Startup, discovery, complete text reads, Unicode calibration, disk spools and candidate GNU work can dominate runtime.

Stable ordinary-input tests establish finite stdout/stderr/status comparisons for captured binaries/platforms. They do not prove all GNU regex, option sequences, encodings, filesystems, concurrent mutations, syscall timing or arbitrary signals.

Text preparation performs additional complete reads and metadata traversal; it can change atime/access events and early-exit I/O relative to GNU. Version checks detect observed changes, not changes occurring after proof and before rg reads.
Native execution is honest interface compatibility for unqualified commands; discarded rg or synthetic calibration is not evidence that native commands were accelerated.

Documentation points at implementation and test inventory rather than embedding a release pass claim; actual packed artifact qualification must reference matching source/artifact identities separately.

evidence.evidenceInterpretation: References identify tests and provenance. This coverage file does not assert that every referenced check passed against a newly packed release.

zeroSearchCategories.contract: Original GNU arguments are forwarded, but no original subject search occurs when GNU performs informational output, zero-count validation or an error before reading subjects. Forwarding does not imply an input search or rg acceleration.
examples: GNU option/pattern failure before subject access

zeroSearchCategories.contract: Preparation can select zero input descriptors; the formatter completes without starting an actual rg search. A proposed rg backend alone earns no actual-input contribution credit.

routingPolicy.default: Direct original GNU before Node/preflight; normal Pi Bash remains unchanged.
routingPolicy.reason: No existing class has a universal wall-time guarantee; explicit experiments preserve semantically qualified rg routes without automatic forcing.
routingPolicy.verification: Verification explicitly enables experimental routes and separately removes/overrides the flag for independent native-default tests.
